summary: Hillis and Steele present data parallel algorithms for fine-grained SIMD machines with general communication, using the Connection Machine as the example. The algorithms cover sums, prefix sums, counting, radix sort, parsing and linked-list operations, and some of their run times are measured on a 65,536-processor machine.
why_read: It is the clearest early statement of the data parallel style, showing how a programmer reasons with one processor per element and general communication.
main_contribution: A set of data parallel algorithms and a programming model with one virtual processor per element and general SEND communication, demonstrated on the Connection Machine.
main_limitation: The authors state that the model suits machines with thousands rather than tens of processors, and most timings come from one 65,536-processor machine.
evaluation_method: Measured run times on a 65,536-processor Connection Machine for selected operations, plus asymptotic analysis under a unit-cost model.
benchmarks: Partial sums, count and enumerate on 65,536 elements (about 200 microseconds each)
Radix sort versus Batcher sort on 65,536 32-bit keys (about 30 ms)

evidence.section: Sum, partial sums, counting and enumerating, radix sort (pp. 1172-1175)
Parsing a regular language and processor-cons (pp. 1175-1177)

notes: Title printed in capitals ('DATA PARALLEL ALGORITHMS'); the catalog differs only in case. First author W.
